record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Establish converse input-to-state stability Lyapunov theorems for broad classes of infinite-dimensional systems beyond the currently covered cases, specifically for general nonlinear systems and for general linear boundary control systems. The goal is to know when ISS necessarily implies the existence of an appropriate ISS Lyapunov function in these settings.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.28. For general nonlinear systems and even for general linear boundary control systems converse ISS Lyapunov theorems are not available now and constitute an important and complex open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider control systems of the form
  ẋ(t) = Ax(t) + f(x(t), u(t)),    x(t) ∈ X,  u ∈ U_c,
where X is a Banach space (the state space), U_c is a space of admissible input functions u: [0, ∞) → U taking values in a Banach space U (typically L^∞ or piecewise continuous functions), and the dynamics are given either by

(a) a general nonlinear evolution equation, where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on X and f: X × U → X (or, more generally, into an extrapolation space) is a nonlinear term ensuring well-posedness of mild solutions, or

(b) a general linear boundary control system, written abstractly as
  ẋ(t) = 𝔄 x(t),    𝔅 x(t) = u(t),
where 𝔄: D(𝔄) ⊂ X → X is a closed linear operator, 𝔅: D(𝔄) → U is a boundary operator, and (𝔄, 𝔅) generates a well-posed boundary control system in the sense of Salamon–Weiss.

Definitions. Let 𝒦 = { γ: ℝ_{≥0} → ℝ_{≥0} : continuous, strictly increasing, γ(0)=0 }, 𝒦_∞ the subclass of unbounded such functions, and 𝒦𝓛 the class of functions β(r,t) that are 𝒦 in r and decay to 0 in t. The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ 𝒦𝓛 and γ ∈ 𝒦_∞ such that, for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t; x_0, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{[0,t]})    for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous function V: X → ℝ_{≥0} is called an ISS Lyapunov function if there exist ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ 𝒦_∞, α ∈ 𝒦_∞, and χ ∈ 𝒦 such that
  ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖)    for all x ∈ X,
and along solutions
  ‖x‖ ≥ χ(‖u‖)   ⟹   V̇(x, u) ≤ −α(‖x‖),
where V̇ is the appropriate (Dini or Lie) derivative along the system.

Problem. Prove (or disprove) the following converse ISS Lyapunov theorems:

(1) For the general nonlinear class (a): if the system is ISS, then there exists a (coercive, possibly Lipschitz continuous) ISS Lyapunov function V: X → ℝ_{≥0}.

(2) For general linear boundary control systems (b): if the system is ISS (with respect to a suitable norm on the input space), then there exists an ISS Lyapunov function V on X.

Determine, in each case, the strongest regularity (continuity, local Lipschitz continuity, smoothness) and the structural form (coercive vs. non-coercive, quadratic when applicable) of the ISS Lyapunov function that can be guaranteed.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed: non-coercive converse Lyapunov theorems for ISS of infinite-dimensional systems have been established (Mironchenko–Wirth and follow-ups), and recent work proves coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded (including boundary) input operators, as well as quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions for analytic linear systems. Counterexamples show that coercive quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions need not exist even for analytic semigroups with bounded inputs. However, fully general converse ISS Lyapunov theorems for arbitrary nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems and for the full class of linear boundary control systems remain unresolved, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals are constructed for regular linear systems with unbounded input operators, covering boundary control settings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work has produced converse-type coercive ISS Lyapunov functional constructions for regular infinite-dimensional linear systems including boundary control.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic ISS Lyapunov functions for linear analytic systems
status_evidence.snippet: ISS of a linear system does not imply existence of a coercive quadratic ISS Lyapunov function even for analytic semigroups with bounded inputs; positive results hold under contraction similarity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial converse results and explicit obstructions are known for linear analytic systems, showing the question is sensitive to structural assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Noncoercive Lyapunov Functions for Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Non-coercive Lipschitz continuous Lyapunov functions are constructed for UGAS infinite-dimensional systems with disturbances, yielding Lyapunov characterizations of ISS.
status_evidence.claim: Non-coercive converse Lyapunov theorems for ISS of broad classes of infinite-dimensional systems have been proved.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists converse ISS Lyapunov theorems for general nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems and for general linear boundary control systems as open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The fully general converse ISS Lyapunov problem was identified as open and remains unresolved in full generality.
